title: Affine norm for a finite law
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a finite measure space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $s\subseteq\mathbb R$ be finite, with $X\in s$ almost everywhere. For $q>0$ and $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the real-valued random-variable norm satisfies $N_q(a+bX)^2=\left(\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)\,|a+bx|^q\right)^{2/q}$.
hypotheses_covered: $s$ is a finite subset of $\mathbb R$
replaced: Let $\mu$ be a finite measure, let $X$ be measurable and supported almost everywhere on a finite $s\subseteq\bbr$, let $q>0$, and let $a,b\in\bbr$. Then $\|a+bX\|_q^2=(\sum_{x\in s}\mu(X=x)|a+bx|^q)^{2/q}$.
